# 01 Accept all four flowchart directions

## Outcome

`flowchart TB`, `flowchart BT`, `flowchart RL` and `flowchart LR` all parse and lay out in the
direction they name. `flowchart TD` keeps working, as an alias of `TB`.

## Why this ticket exists

`FLOWCHART_HEADER_RE` is `/^flowchart\s+(TD|LR)\s*$/`, so `flowchart TB` — the spelling Mermaid's
own documentation leads with — is rejected with `Expected "flowchart TD" or "flowchart LR"`. The
same document's `classDiagram` sibling has accepted all four since the class board. A file that
renders in Mermaid should render here; today a one-word header decides otherwise.

The direction only ever travels one way (header → `Direction` → `layoutGraph` → dagre's `rankdir`)
and is never rendered or re-emitted, so normalizing `TD` to `TB` at the parser costs nothing and
buys one vocabulary downstream.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `render()` on a `flowchart TB` document returns an SVG and no diagnostics, and its layout
  matches the same document written `flowchart TD` exactly.
- [x] `flowchart BT` and `flowchart RL` lay out in those directions — assert against node
  coordinates, not just the absence of diagnostics.
- [x] `Direction` in `contracts.ts` is `"TB" | "BT" | "LR" | "RL"`, and no value of `"TD"` survives
  parsing: a parsed `flowchart TD` document reports `direction: "TB"`.
- [x] `rankDirectionFor` in `layoutGraph.ts` is deleted — with `TD` normalized away, the flowchart
  adapter passes `graph.direction` to `layoutDirectedGraph` unchanged.
- [x] The unrecognized-header diagnostics in `parseFlowchart` and `parseSiren` name the accepted
  spellings, and the empty-document diagnostic in `parseSiren` does too.
- [x] `CONTEXT.md` gains a `Direction` entry stating the four values and that `TD` is an alias, and
  its `Diagram kind` entry no longer says `flowchart TD|LR`.
- [x] Existing flowchart tests that construct `direction: "TD"` are updated to `"TB"` rather than
  the type being widened to keep them compiling.

## Test seam

`render()` and `parseSiren`/`parseFlowchart`. The behavior is in the header text, so a test that
hand-builds a `FlowchartDocument` cannot catch a regex that still rejects `TB` — go through the
source string.
